drills.purpose: Fixes pre-rotation and correct edge on Lutz and Flip jumps
steps: Skate forward on an outside edge building moderate speed
Execute a clean three-turn from forward outside to backward inside edge
Hold the backward inside edge for a count of 2 before any takeoff action
Feel the edge and resist any rotation of the hip or shoulder
Repeat continuously down the length of the rink
coach_cues: Keep weight on the heel of the blade after the three-turn
Square shoulders to the direction of travel
Hip must stay closed — do not open into the jump
Think: edge FIRST, then jump
common_mistakes: Pre-rotating the hip before the three-turn is complete
Leaning too far forward causing a flat or inside edge
Rushing off the back edge — not holding long enough
progressions: Start with two-foot landing after a waltz jump entry
Add a single Flip or Lutz with correct edge focus
Progress to double, then triple with entry focus
drills.video_description: Skater approaches on a back outside edge, executes a clean three-turn to back inside edge, holds for 2 counts, then initiates takeoff

drills.purpose: Fixes check-out technique and free leg position on landing
steps: Stand facing the wall with arms extended touching it lightly
Jump straight up from two feet, pulling arms into landing position
On landing, swing right arm and leg back in a check-out position
Hold the landing position for 3 seconds
Progress to turning 180 degrees then 360 degrees
coach_cues: Landing arm sweeps back like a wing checking rotation
Free leg kicks back and holds — do not let it swing forward
Absorb landing through bent knee — quiet landing
Eyes look forward on landing, not down
common_mistakes: Arms stay in air position too long — must check immediately
Free leg swings forward causing forward fall
Stiff knee on landing — leads to injuries and two-footed landings
progressions: Two-foot jump and hold landing position
Add quarter turn, then half turn
drills.video_description: Skater stands near wall, executes controlled rotation jump, lands in perfect check-out position with free leg extended back

drills.name_ar: تمرين تثبيت الهبوط على قدم واحدة
drills.purpose: Fixes landing position and eliminates two-foot landings
drills.repetitions: Hold each landing for 3 seconds, 15 reps
steps: Execute any single jump (waltz jump, toe loop, Salchow)
Land on outside edge of right foot (or left for left-handed skaters)
Immediately hold the landing position: free leg back, arms in check
Count to 3 while holding balance on one foot
Glide out smoothly before attempting next jump
coach_cues: Landing knee bent at 45 degrees minimum
Free hip down — do not hike the hip up
Eyes forward — looking down causes forward fall
Shoulder over the landing foot for balance
common_mistakes: Immediately putting down the free foot (two-foot landing habit)
Arm check too weak — rotation continues after landing
Landing on flat blade instead of outside edge
progressions: Start with waltz jump — simplest landing to hold
Progress to doubles while maintaining 3-count hold
Competition context: hold for the duration of the musical phrase
drills.video_description: Skater jumps and freezes in textbook landing position, demonstrating perfect check-out with free leg extended back at hip height

drills.purpose: Builds muscle memory for correct toe pick timing and takeoff mechanics
steps: Skate backward on outside edge preparing for toe pick jumps (Flip/Lutz/Toe Loop)
Plant toe pick firmly and feel the vaulting sensation upward
Execute only the takeoff — jump to minimal height — land on two feet
Immediately reset and repeat without skating away
Focus entirely on the mechanics of the takeoff, not the air or landing
coach_cues: Toe pick plants behind and to the side — not underneath the body
Drive the free leg UP on the takeoff — knee leads the lift
Takeoff knee bends then SNAPS straight for maximum power
Upper body stays calm — the legs do the work
common_mistakes: Toe pick too close to the skating foot (causes stumbling)
Leaning forward over the toe pick (reduces height)
Inconsistent toe pick depth (different result each time)
progressions: Slow motion single toe picks standing nearly still
Normal skating speed with rapid consecutive takeoffs
drills.video_description: Skater performs rapid consecutive toe pick takeoffs in a line down the ice, focusing purely on the explosive upward drive of each takeoff

drills.purpose: Develops the Axel approach edge and back outside edge quality
steps: Step onto a back outside edge skating a large circle
Hold single back outside edge for the full circle without touching down
Arms in skating position: one forward, one back
Knee deeply bent, tracing a clean circle in the ice
Look over the shoulder in the direction of travel
coach_cues: Deep knee bend maintains the edge and prevents slipping off
Free leg extended back at hip height — parallel to ice
Ankle must not roll in or out — keep the edge clean
Circle should be 3-4 meters diameter for proper training effect
common_mistakes: Circle shrinking or spiraling — means edge is deteriorating
Hopping off the edge to reset balance
Free foot dragging on ice
progressions: Two-foot back outside edge circles first
Enter the circle from a step for Axel simulation
drills.video_description: Skater carves deep back outside edge circles, body in perfect skating posture, tracing consistent arc in the ice

drills.purpose: Fixes the Flutz (wrong edge) by training correct outside edge on Lutz
steps: Skate a long back outside edge approach from the red line
Coach or skater places a hand on the left hip to prevent rotation
Feel that the left shoulder stays back (counter to direction of jump)
Hold the edge and feel it deepen — back OUTSIDE not inside
Execute the Lutz pick and maintain the counter-rotation feeling
coach_cues: Left arm and shoulder stay BACK — do not open toward the jump
Think: skating on the outside of the left foot, not inside
The more the shoulder opens, the more the edge flattens
Video check: pause the approach to see edge shadow on ice
common_mistakes: Opening the left shoulder which flattens or rolls the edge to inside
Rushing the approach — not holding the outside edge long enough
Looking back at the pick spot which causes rotation
progressions: Practice the approach edge only without jumping
Add a single Lutz with coach holding hip
Double and triple Lutz with edge checks
drills.video_description: Skater executes long Lutz approach with coach providing tactile feedback to maintain outside edge, countering the common flutz habit

drills.purpose: Safe environment for attempting triples and quads, builds height confidence
drills.equipment: jump harness, overhead rig, qualified spotter
steps: Fit skater in harness with qualified coach operating the overhead system
Begin with supported singles to establish air position
Progress to doubles with partial assistance (just safety, no lifting)
For triples/quads: coach provides lift assistance on takeoff phase
Gradually reduce assistance as skater's confidence and rotation speed increase
coach_cues: The harness catches you — commit fully to the rotation
Pull arms in tight: faster pull = faster rotation
Head stays up — chin slightly up helps rotation
Trust the system: fall attempts are completely safe
common_mistakes: Cheating the entry edge because harness provides false security
Not pulling arms in tightly enough
Psychological dependence on harness — must wean off gradually
progressions: Full support: harness carries skater through rotation
Partial support: harness only prevents falls
Safety only: harness present but not assisting
drills.video_description: Skater in harness system executes triple Axel with coach assistance, focusing on rotation mechanics and landing position without fear of falling

drills.name_ar: القفز على قدمين إلى قفز منفرد
drills.purpose: Teaches basic air position and rotation feeling for beginning jumpers
steps: Jump from two feet rotating half turn in the air
Pull arms and free leg in tight during the air
Land on two feet, then progress to one-foot landings
Increase to full rotation (360 degrees)
Add speed by approaching from crossovers
coach_cues: Jump UP not around — height first, then rotation
Arms pull in at the peak of the jump — not on the way up
Tight free leg in the air prevents wide landing
Land on the whole blade, then shift to outside edge
common_mistakes: Jumping around instead of up — produces flat low jumps
Arms too wide in the air — slows rotation
Looking down on the jump — breaks body alignment
progressions: Full single jump with proper edge
drills.video_description: Young skater practices two-foot jumps on ice, learning the fundamental sensation of rotation and air position before progressing to proper singles

drills.purpose: Axel preparation drill — develops forward takeoff mechanics and half rotation
drills.repetitions: 4 sets of 8 repetitions in a row
steps: Enter from a forward outside edge on left foot (counter-clockwise jumpers)
Step onto left forward outside edge, swing right leg forward and up
Take off from the left forward outside edge
Rotate half turn in the air
Land on right backward outside edge
Chain consecutive waltz jumps without stopping
coach_cues: The swing leg drives the takeoff — knee up high
Take off from the TOE of the blade, not the heel
Land with knee bent — spring landing, not crash landing
The forward takeoff is the ONLY difference from other jumps
common_mistakes: Taking off from the flat or heel of the blade
Not completing the full half rotation — landing forward
Swing leg goes back instead of forward on takeoff
progressions: Step into waltz jump from standstill
drills.video_description: Skater executes continuous waltz jump sequences in a straight line, each with perfect forward outside edge takeoff and controlled backward outside edge landing

drills.purpose: Develops air flexibility, leg strength, and artistic expression for PCS
steps: Approach from forward stroking, building moderate speed
Take off from left toe pick (similar to Flip takeoff)
In the air, kick right leg forward and left leg back simultaneously
Reach maximum split position at the peak of the jump
Bring legs together and land on right outside edge
coach_cues: Split must be at 180 degrees minimum for maximum GOE
Toes pointed at the peak of the split
Upper body stays upright — do not collapse forward
This is a PCS element — expression on the face matters
common_mistakes: Split not reaching 180 degrees — looks shallow and earns lower GOE
Collapsing upper body forward on split
Landing on two feet due to poor air position transition
progressions: Full split jump on ice with rotation
drills.video_description: Skater executes beautiful split jump with legs extended to 180 degrees at the peak, demonstrating excellent flexibility and artistic quality

drills.purpose: Isolates the back outside edge for Loop jump and develops correct air position
steps: Skate backward on a right back outside edge
Draw the free foot to the side and across — feet parallel
Feel both feet creating the locked entry position
Jump from the back outside edge only — no toe pick
Rotate in a tight position, land on right back outside edge
coach_cues: Entry position: feet together, arms crossed or in front of chest
Jump from the heel of the blade, not the toe
Wrap both arms into the body for the rotation
Landing knee bent deeply to absorb the back-weighted landing
common_mistakes: Jumping from flat edge instead of outside edge
Using toe pick to assist the takeoff (makes it a Toe Loop)
Arms too loose in the air — creates wobbly rotation
drills.video_description: Skater in locked entry position with feet parallel jumps a clean loop, demonstrating the back outside edge takeoff with no toe pick assistance

drills.purpose: Isolates back inside edge for Flip to prevent Lip (wrong edge) habit
steps: Skate backward on a left back inside edge in a curve
Feel the inside edge deeply — weight on inside of blade
Hold the edge without wobbling for 2 full counts
Pick with right toe, keeping the left inside edge until last moment
Execute the Flip jump, focusing on maintaining the inside edge
coach_cues: Inside edge means weight on the inner side of the foot
Think: lean slightly into the circle before the pick
The pick should feel like a vaulting pole — straight up
Video the approach — a flat or outside edge is visible in the ice tracing
common_mistakes: Rolling onto outside or flat edge just before the pick (the Lip)
Leaning back into the jump causing the edge to flatten
Picking too close to the skating foot
progressions: Practice the inside edge approach without jumping
Small Flip jump focusing only on the edge
Full single Flip with edge focus
Double and triple Flip with video review
drills.video_description: Skater traces visible back inside edge in the ice before Flip takeoff, demonstrating proper edge execution with tracing visible to judge angle cameras

drills.purpose: Develops correct speed, posture, and control before takeoff for all jumps
steps: Begin from a standstill or slow speed
Build controlled speed with crossovers entering the jump corner
Transition onto the correct approach edge for the jump
Hold the approach edge for 3 counts
Execute the jump from this controlled entry
coach_cues: Speed should be fast enough to jump with power, slow enough to control
Approach edge must be deep — not a flat glide
Head up — eyes on the horizon, not the ice
Relax the upper body — tension kills jump height
common_mistakes: Too fast on entry — leads to rushed preparation and edge errors
Too slow — insufficient energy for proper height
Flat approach edge — no curve, no control
progressions: Stationary to jump approach only (no jump)
Add the jump from a very controlled entry
drills.video_description: Skater executes a smooth controlled approach to a jump corner, demonstrating the decelerate-to-load then explode-up technique

drills.purpose: Develops centering ability and blade balance for all spins
steps: Stand on left foot on a back outside edge
Circle slowly, feeling the sweet spot of the blade
Move the pressure forward toward the ball of the foot
Find the spin position: front-center of blade (rocker)
Hold this position as long as possible without moving
coach_cues: The spinning spot is just behind the ball of the foot — not the toe pick
Press DOWN into the ice — do not lift up
Free hip must be down and in — not hiking
Think: grow taller while pressing into the ice
common_mistakes: Spinning on the toe pick — creates scratchy, noisy, decentered spin
Too far back on the heel — spin travels backward across the ice
Free hip lifted — causes the whole body to tilt
progressions: Two-foot spin to find the sweet spot
Scratch spin entry from backward push
drills.video_description: Skater finds the perfect blade balance point for spinning, demonstrating the subtle weight placement that allows for a perfectly centered spin

drills.purpose: Increases RPM and teaches various entry options for scratch spin
steps: Entry 1: Backward crossover entry into forward scratch
Entry 2: Three-turn entry (forward outside, three-turn, back spin entry)
Entry 3: Mohawk entry for variety
Entry 4: Jump entry (flying spin)
For each entry, count rotations and note which gives most speed
coach_cues: The entry must be committed — no hesitation as speed becomes spin
Gather the arms smoothly — sudden pull kills centering
Shoulders stay level throughout the entry
The faster the crossover approach, the more potential RPM
common_mistakes: Entry too slow — insufficient angular momentum to spin well
Arms yanked in suddenly — causes body to tip
Leaning forward on entry — travels forward
progressions: Slow two-foot spin to establish the feel
drills.video_description: Skater demonstrates multiple entry options for scratch spin — backward crossovers, three-turn entry, and flying entry — comparing RPM achieved

drills.purpose: Develops body alignment for back scratch spin and increases rotation speed
steps: Enter a back spin from a forward three-turn
Establish balance on the right back inside edge
Bring free foot in to ankle height, then cross it over
Pull arms into a tight cross-arm position at chest level
Count rotations and aim to increase each session
coach_cues: Back spin is on back INSIDE edge — weight slightly inside
Crossing the free foot is what creates the speed increase
Arms cross: right arm crosses left at chest level
Head stays up — chin level, not tilted
common_mistakes: Back spin on the wrong edge (outside edge causes traveling)
Free foot only comes to ankle — needs to cross for max RPM
Arms too far out from body during pull-in phase
progressions: Two-foot back spin to find the back inside edge
One-foot back spin with free leg out
Pull in to back scratch position
Flying back camel to back scratch combination
drills.video_description: Skater spins a controlled back scratch, demonstrating the back inside edge balance and the arm pull-in that dramatically increases rotation speed

drills.purpose: Develops hip and back flexibility required for a strong camel spin position
steps: Stand at barre, hold with one hand for balance
Stand on left foot and extend right leg back to hip height
Hip must be OPEN — right hip rotates up and back
Upper body tilts forward to 90 degrees (T-position)
Hold for 10 seconds, maintaining hip rotation and leg height
coach_cues: Hip rotation is everything in the camel: open it like a door
Think: show the bottom of the free foot to the ceiling
Upper body and free leg must be parallel to floor for a perfect camel
Engage the core to maintain the position without wobbling
common_mistakes: Hip closed (facing down) — makes the free leg look dropped
Free leg below hip height — not a level camel
Upper body too high — not reaching full 90 degree tilt
drills.video_description: Skater demonstrates camel position off-ice at the barre — right hip fully open, free leg at hip height, upper body at 90 degrees in textbook form

drills.purpose: Develops flexibility and strength for a deep, low sit spin position
steps: Stand with feet parallel, shoulder width apart
Lower into deep squat until thigh is below parallel to floor
Extend right leg straight out to the side (skating free leg)
Balance on left foot with right leg fully extended
Hold for 5 seconds, maintaining thigh below parallel
coach_cues: Thigh must be below parallel — above is not a proper sit spin
Free leg fully extended and off the floor the entire time
Back stays upright — do not hunch forward
Ankle flexibility helps enormously — point the free foot toe
common_mistakes: Thigh not below parallel — the sit spin will be called too high
Free leg not fully extended — a bent free leg loses level features
Falling forward — core is not engaged enough
progressions: One-foot squat with free leg extended
Balance on balance board in sit position
On-ice sit spin, lowering gradually over multiple sessions
drills.video_description: Skater holds perfect sit spin position off-ice — thigh clearly below parallel, free leg extended, back upright, demonstrating the required depth

drills.purpose: Develops the jump into a camel spin with correct air position and entry
steps: Approach from backward crossovers building speed
Step onto left forward outside edge
Jump from the left outside edge into the camel position
In the air, kick the right leg up and back into camel angle
Land on right back outside edge and spin in camel position immediately
coach_cues: The jump is a waltz jump — forward outside edge takeoff
Free leg must be in camel position BEFORE landing
Do not spin forward — the entry must convert to a back spin quickly
Think: jump forward, fly like a bird, land in camel
common_mistakes: Landing in forward spin instead of backward camel position
Not enough height in the jump to achieve camel position in air
Camel position not achieved until after landing — looks like a stumble
progressions: Small flying camel entry without full height
Full flying camel to centered camel spin
drills.video_description: Skater executes a flying camel entry — leaping forward and achieving full camel position in the air before landing smoothly into a centered camel spin

drills.purpose: Develops shoulder and back flexibility for Biellmann spin position
drills.repetitions: 3 sets of 10 stretches, hold 20 seconds each
steps: Lie face down on mat, arms at sides
Bend right knee, reaching back to hold the right foot with right hand
Use a stretching strap to assist — loop around right foot, hold overhead
Gently pull the foot toward and over the head
Progress over weeks to reach foot to head and eventually past the head
coach_cues: This is a long-term flexibility progression — do not force it
Shoulders must rotate to allow the hands to reach overhead
Core engaged to protect the lower back during the stretch
Weekly progress photos show improvement that daily practice misses
common_mistakes: Forcing the stretch — causes shoulder and back injuries
Only stretching one side — the non-dominant side is equally important
Not maintaining the stretch — consistency is key, 7 days/week
progressions: Standard back kick flexibility — foot to head height
Over-head flexibility — foot above head level
Biellmann position off-ice with strap assist
drills.video_description: Skater demonstrates progressive Biellmann flexibility training with a strap, showing the multi-month progression from basic back kick to full Biellmann position

drills.purpose: Develops back arch and head position for layback spin (primarily ladies)
steps: Stand upright, arms in spin position
Tilt the head back until looking at the ceiling behind you
Let the upper back arch backward, arms flowing back
Engage core to protect the lumbar spine
Hold for 15 seconds breathing normally
coach_cues: The arch comes from the upper back, not the lower back
Head goes back fully — you should see the wall behind you
Arms flow gracefully back — not thrown back
Free leg position options: attitude, kick, arabesque angle
common_mistakes: Arching from the lower back (lumbar) — causes back pain and injuries
Not tilting the head far enough — looks like a forward lean
Losing the spinning position while trying to achieve the layback
progressions: Layback position against wall for support
Layback while slowly rotating on floor
drills.video_description: Skater holds beautiful layback position off-ice — full head tilt, upper back arch, arms flowing gracefully back in elegant artistic position

drills.purpose: Develops smooth, fast foot changes and position transitions in combination spins
steps: Enter a camel spin — spin 4+ rotations in camel position
Step forward to change foot: step onto left foot smoothly
Immediately establish a forward camel or sit position on the left
Transition to sit, then stand, then pull up to back scratch
Entire combination should have no deceleration between positions
coach_cues: The step-forward must be fast — hesitation loses speed
New foot must land on spin blade spot immediately
Aim for 4 positions with 4 rotations minimum each for Level 4
Centering is priority — a traveling combination spin loses levels
common_mistakes: Deceleration between positions — causes the spin to stop
Traveling on the change of foot
Not completing minimum rotations in each position
progressions: Full competition combination with all required features
drills.video_description: Skater executes a complete combination spin through camel, sit, upright, and change-foot positions, maintaining consistent speed throughout all transitions

drills.purpose: Develops edge quality, power generation, and skating flow without stroking
steps: Start skating forward on left outside edge in a large curve
Without putting down the right foot, generate power by pressing the left knee in and out
Feel the edge grip and release as you pump through the knee
Alternate to right outside edge, then backward edges
Goal: accelerate down the rink using only edge power pulls
coach_cues: The power comes from the knee bend and ankle pressure, not the arms
Edge angle must be aggressive — at least 30 degrees
Free leg stays off the ice the entire length
Sound of the blade should be a clean swish, not a scrape
common_mistakes: Using arms to generate momentum — cheating the drill
Letting free foot touch down
Edge too shallow — not enough angle to create power
progressions: Alternating edge power pulls in figure-8 pattern
drills.video_description: Skater accelerates down the ice using pure edge power pulls — no stroking — demonstrating exceptional edge quality and skating skill

drills.purpose: Develops deep outside edge quality, body position, and edge sustainability
drills.repetitions: 4 sets down the length of the rink
steps: Push onto left forward outside edge
Hold the edge for a full semi-circle (half the width of the rink)
Step to right forward outside edge without losing flow
Continue alternating — tracing two connected half-circles down the ice
Arms: forward arm on the side of the edge, back arm trailing
coach_cues: Each lobe should be equal size — consistency is what judges measure
Deep knee bend maintains the edge — straight knee kills it
Head looks in the direction of travel — not down at the ice
The tracing on the ice shows the truth — look back and evaluate
common_mistakes: Lobes unequal in size or shape
Rushing the step — skipping the full semi-circle
Arms out of skating position — drifting too far out or in
progressions: Forward outside edges (starting point for all skaters)
Edges with free leg extended in spiral position
drills.video_description: Skater traces perfect consecutive outside edges — each lobe identical in size, deep knee bend, clean tracing visible in the ice

drills.purpose: Develops edge control through turns and is fundamental to step sequences
steps: Skate forward on left outside edge in a curve
Execute a three-turn: turn from forward outside to backward inside
Hold the back inside edge and continue the curve
Step to other foot and repeat in opposite direction
Create a continuous serpentine pattern down the ice
coach_cues: The turn must be a POINT on the ice — not a scrape or slide
After the turn, hold the back edge — resist stepping out immediately
Shoulder rotation executes the three-turn — hip and knee follow
Look over the shoulder in the direction of travel after the turn
common_mistakes: Flat edge before and/or after the turn
Scraping through the turn instead of a clean point
Stepping out immediately after the turn — not holding the back edge
drills.video_description: Skater executes a flowing series of three-turns creating a smooth serpentine pattern, each turn a clean precise point in the ice

drills.purpose: Develops turn variety for step sequences and improves transition quality
steps: Skate forward on left outside edge in a curve
Execute a Mohawk: step to right forward inside edge (change of foot, same direction)
Continue from the inside edge, building speed
Execute a Choctaw: step to left backward outside edge (change of direction and foot)
Combine in series: Mohawk-Choctaw-Mohawk-Choctaw
coach_cues: Mohawk steps must be light and quick — not heavy stomps
The step in a Mohawk: new foot steps parallel, then heels together
Choctaw requires a hip opening — this takes flexibility
Maintain ice coverage — steps should move you through space
common_mistakes: Steps too close together — not covering ice
Hesitating before the Choctaw — a pause breaks the flow
Not maintaining speed through the sequence
drills.video_description: Skater executes fluid Mohawk-Choctaw sequence maintaining speed and flow, demonstrating the hip flexibility required for quality Choctaw steps

drills.purpose: Adds difficult turns to step sequences for higher GOE and Level 4
steps: Skate forward on outside edge in a curve
Execute a bracket turn: turn into the curve (as opposed to three-turn which turns out of curve)
The turn point makes a bracket shape — ] — in the ice
Hold the resulting back outside edge (for forward outside bracket)
Practice forward outside, forward inside, backward outside, backward inside brackets
coach_cues: Bracket is the OPPOSITE of a three-turn — turn INTO the circle
It feels counter-intuitive — the body must counter-rotate
Upper body counter-rotation is what makes brackets difficult
A clean bracket point is worth significant GOE in step sequences
common_mistakes: Executing a three-turn instead of a bracket (turning the wrong direction)
No counter-rotation — the bracket has no check
Stepping out immediately — must hold the resulting edge
progressions: Brackets in combination with other turns
drills.video_description: Skater executes bracket turns demonstrating the counter-intuitive technique — turning into the circle rather than out of it, creating the distinctive bracket shape in the ice

drills.purpose: Adds the most difficult turns (counters and rockers) for Level 4 step sequences
steps: Rocker: skate on outside edge, turn to inside edge while continuing same direction (reverse of three-turn logic)
Counter: skate on outside edge, turn to outside edge while reversing direction
Practice each independently at slow speed first
Combine in a pattern: Rocker-Counter-Rocker-Counter
Build to full speed with all turns in a straight line
coach_cues: Counters and Rockers require extreme edge control and balance
These are Level 4 features — each one in a step sequence raises the level
The body must remain over the skating foot throughout — no hip shifting
Weekly video review helps identify subtle technique errors
common_mistakes: Stepping out of the edge to execute the turn — must stay on edge throughout
Using the arms to force the turn — should be done with the body core
Turns too slow — competition-speed execution requires the turns to be quick
progressions: In combination with other turns at competition speed
drills.video_description: Skater executes rocker and counter turns at competition speed — each turn precise and controlled, demonstrating the highest level of turning technique in figure skating

drills.purpose: Develops twizzles for Ice Dance, free skating step sequences, and choreographic elements
steps: Approach on a forward outside edge with speed
Raise free leg to a bent position at hip height
Initiate rotation while traveling on the edge
Complete 1-3 rotations while traveling in a straight line
Exit on back outside edge and continue skating
coach_cues: Twizzles travel across the ice — they are not spins
The edge must be maintained throughout the rotation
Arm position: close to body to maintain rotation speed
Keep head up — dropping the head causes the twizzle to stop
common_mistakes: Stopping in place instead of traveling — that is a spin, not a twizzle
Wobbling off the edge mid-rotation
Arms too wide — slows the rotation
progressions: Single rotation twizzle from slow approach
Sequence of three consecutive twizzles in a line
drills.video_description: Skater executes a traveling twizzle sequence — rotating 2-3 times while moving across the ice, maintaining balance and edge throughout the turns

drills.purpose: Develops the Flip and Loop jump entry control on the back inside edge
steps: Skate backward on left inside edge in a curve
Execute a three-turn: backward inside to forward outside
Hold the forward outside edge and continue the curve
Step to right back inside edge and repeat
Create serpentine pattern down the ice
coach_cues: Back inside three-turn is the hardest three-turn variant — be patient
The turn point must be clean and sharp, not a scrape
After the turn, hold forward outside edge before stepping to next edge
This edge is the exact approach to Flip and Loop jumps
common_mistakes: Stepping out immediately after the turn instead of holding
Losing the inside edge before the turn (flattening)
The turn becoming a stumble due to unsteady back inside edge
progressions: Forward outside three-turns first (build the concept)
drills.video_description: Skater executes series of backward inside three-turns at increasing speed — the foundation for Flip and Loop jump entries

drills.purpose: Designs optimal step sequence layout using maximum ice coverage
steps: Draw the ice surface on paper and mark entry and exit points
Plan the sequence to use the full width and length of the rink
Include a minimum of 7 different turns for Level 4
Mark where the difficult turns (brackets, counters, rockers) appear
Walk through at slow speed, then full speed
coach_cues: A Level 4 StSq requires: 7+ different turns, steps, 3 difficult turns minimum
Ice coverage is a GOE bullet — use the whole rink
The sequence must connect to the music phrasing
Transitions in and out of the sequence affect PCS Transitions score
common_mistakes: Step sequence staying in one part of the ice — poor ice coverage
Repeating the same turns — not enough variety for higher levels
Step sequence too simple for the skater's claimed level
progressions: Simple Circular Step Sequence (older rules format) for basics
Add elements gradually to build toward Level 4
drills.video_description: Coach and skater review the ice pattern drawn on a whiteboard, planning the optimal step sequence layout for maximum ice coverage and Level 4 achievement

drills.purpose: Maintains and increases speed throughout the step sequence for GOE
steps: Enter the step sequence from a standstill or slow speed (baseline)
Run through the entire step sequence, noting where speed is lost
Identify the 2-3 transitions that cause the most deceleration
Drill those specific transitions until they generate power
Re-run the full sequence and compare entry vs exit speed
coach_cues: Speed INCREASE through a step sequence is a positive GOE bullet
Each step should push you forward — edges generate power
Use knee bend and ankle pressure, not arm swinging, for power
Exiting faster than you entered shows exceptional Skating Skills
common_mistakes: Decelerating through turns — not pushing through the edge
Over-choreographed arms that take energy away from feet
Steps too small — tiny steps cannot generate power
progressions: Slow motion step sequence with focus on power generation
Full speed with additional arm expression
drills.video_description: Skater executes step sequence entering at normal speed and visibly accelerating through the sequence, exiting with more speed than at entry

drills.purpose: Maximizes turn count in step sequence for Level 4 achievement
steps: Plan a sequence with: 2 three-turns, 2 brackets, 2 counters or rockers, 2 Mohawks, 1 Choctaw
Execute all turns consecutively in a linked pattern
Must include turns on both forward and backward edges
Must include turns on both inside and outside edges
All 7+ turns must appear in a single step sequence
coach_cues: Level 4 step sequence has 7 DIFFERENT turn types — not just 7 total turns
After every turn, the connecting edge is as important as the turn itself
The difficulty of the turn combination raises GOE from +1 to +3 or more
Memorize the sequence so all focus is on quality during competition
common_mistakes: Only using three-turns and Mohawks — limits to Level 2 maximum
Poor connection between turns — gaps or hesitations
Turns executed on the wrong edge
drills.video_description: Skater executes full Level 4 turn combination — seven different turn types in a flowing, connected sequence with no hesitation between turns

drills.purpose: Develops the arm-leg-body coordination that contributes to PCS Performance
steps: Skate forward stroking to music
Add arm movements that coordinate with each stroke and step
Arms move in opposition: right arm forward when left foot pushes
Add head movements synchronized with arm movements
Layer in expression — make the arms reflect the music
coach_cues: Arms are the face of the step sequence — audiences watch the arms
Arm movements should finish on the musical beat
The arms do not move the skater — they express the music
Film yourself — arm movements often look bigger in your head than in reality
common_mistakes: Arms too stiff and mechanical — no organic expression
Arms moving independently of the music — off the beat
Over-choreographed at the expense of skating quality
progressions: Add simple arm movements on the beat
Add head and upper body movement
drills.video_description: Skater performs step sequence with beautifully coordinated arms and body movement perfectly synchronized to the music

drills.purpose: Develops rotation speed and jump rhythm for consistent triples
steps: Standard double-under jump rope: rope passes twice per jump
Advance to triple-under: rope passes three times per jump
Focus on maximum height, tight air position, fast arm rotation
Triple-under timing mirrors the rotation speed needed for triple jumps
Increase set length as endurance improves
coach_cues: Maximum height on each jump — height is the foundation
Arms tight to body while rope rotates — like the arms in a jump
Consistent timing between jumps — no rushing
Triple-under takes months to develop — be patient
common_mistakes: Not enough height — cannot complete three rope passes in low jump
Arms too wide — rope hits the feet
Irregular rhythm — some jumps higher, some lower
progressions: Double-under consistent for 30 in a row
Triple-under consistent for 10 in a row
drills.video_description: Skater executes triple-under jump rope with maximum height and tight body position, demonstrating the rotational speed equivalent to triple jump timing

drills.purpose: Builds rotational core power essential for quad and triple jump height and speed
steps: Stand sideways 1.5 meters from a solid wall
Hold medicine ball at hip level on the far side from the wall
Rotate explosively, throwing the ball against the wall
Catch the rebound and rotate back for immediate next throw
Both directions equally important — non-dominant side often weaker
coach_cues: Power comes from the hips and core — not the arms
The rotation feels like the first half of a jump's rotation
Maintain athletic stance — do not let the rotation lift the heels
Use as heavy a ball as can be thrown with full speed
common_mistakes: Using arms instead of rotating the trunk — misses the training target
Not using the rebound — the catch is also a training stimulus
Too light a ball — no resistance training effect
progressions: Light ball, slow rotation (learning the movement)
Add a squat before the throw for combined power
drills.video_description: Skater throws medicine ball explosively against wall in rotational pattern, demonstrating the hip and core power that drives jump rotation

drills.name_ar: قرفصاء على قدم واحدة على قرص بوسو
drills.purpose: Develops ankle stability, balance, and single-leg strength for landings
steps: Stand on flat side of Bosu ball on left foot (dome side down for instability)
Extend right leg slightly in front, simulating landing position
Lower slowly into a single-leg squat to 90 degrees
Pause at bottom for 2 seconds
Drive back up to standing, maintaining balance throughout
coach_cues: Knee tracks over the middle toe — do not let it cave in
Use the ankle to stabilize — the instability is the training
Hands on hips — not holding anything for balance
Progress to eyes closed once stable on eyes-open version
common_mistakes: Knee caving inward (valgus) — increases injury risk and indicates hip weakness
Holding onto something for balance — removes the training stimulus
Not going deep enough — above 90 degrees is insufficient
progressions: Jump and land single-leg on Bosu ball
target_elements: all landings — ankle and knee stability
drills.video_description: Skater performs single-leg squats on Bosu ball — developing the ankle and knee stability essential for consistent jump landings on the ice

drills.purpose: Builds hip flexor and glute strength for jump height and free leg position
steps: Attach resistance band around ankle and anchor to a sturdy point at hip height
Stand facing the anchor, left foot banded
Kick left leg forward (hip flexor) against the resistance
Control the return movement slowly
Turn away from anchor: kick the leg back (glute) against resistance
Turn sideways: kick leg to the side (abductor)
coach_cues: All kicks are controlled — no swinging or momentum
Standing leg stays strong — do not let the hip tilt on each kick
The angle of the kick should match the jump swing leg angle
Slow return (eccentric phase) is as important as the kick
common_mistakes: Using momentum to kick — takes the load off the target muscle
Hip tilting on the standing side
Range of motion too small — kick to full extension
progressions: Add a balance challenge: standing on unstable surface while kicking
drills.video_description: Skater performs resistance band kick exercises in all directions, developing the hip strength essential for powerful jump takeoffs and high free leg positions

drills.purpose: Builds anti-rotation core strength essential for spin centering and jump control
steps: TRX Fallout: hold handles, lean forward and extend arms overhead, resist the pull
TRX Atomic Pushup: feet in straps, perform pushup then draw knees to chest
TRX Single-leg Squat: one foot in strap behind, single-leg squat on standing leg
TRX Plank with rotation: plank position, rotate one arm toward ceiling
TRX Pike: feet in straps, pike hips straight up maintaining straight legs
coach_cues: TRX fallout mimics the anti-rotation needed for a centered spin
Keep hips level in all exercises — hip drop defeats the purpose
Breathe out on the effort phase of each exercise
Adjust strap length as needed — steeper angle = easier
common_mistakes: Hips sagging in plank exercises — disengages the core
Moving too fast — momentum replaces muscle engagement
Not using full range of motion
progressions: Stable surface equivalent exercises (floor plank, etc.)
TRX exercises at moderate difficulty angle
TRX exercises at challenging difficulty angle
Add rotation or instability to each exercise
drills.video_description: Skater performs full TRX circuit including fallout, atomic pushup, and rotating plank — core stability work that directly translates to spin centering

drills.purpose: Injury prevention — releases tightness in the IT band that causes knee pain in skaters
steps: Lie on right side, right thigh on foam roller, just below the hip
Support upper body on right forearm
Roll slowly from hip to just above the knee — 2-3 second passes
Find tender spots and pause on them for 30-60 seconds
Complete from hip to knee, then reverse
coach_cues: This will hurt initially — that is normal and indicates tightness
Breathe into the tender spots to release the tissue
The pain should decrease over 2-4 weeks of consistent rolling
Do this BEFORE and AFTER ice sessions for maximum benefit
common_mistakes: Rolling too fast — the tissue needs slow sustained pressure to release
Rolling the knee itself — never roll directly on a joint
Skipping the tender spots — those are exactly where you need to pause
drills.video_description: Skater demonstrates IT band foam rolling technique — slow methodical rolling from hip to knee with pauses on tender spots for effective tissue release

drills.purpose: Prevents ankle injuries and improves blade control by strengthening ankle stabilizers
steps: Sit on edge of a bench, feet hanging free
Wrap Theraband around foot, anchor the other end to a fixed point
Plantar flexion: point the foot down against resistance (push down)
Dorsiflexion: pull the foot up against resistance
Inversion: turn foot inward against resistance
Eversion: turn foot outward against resistance
coach_cues: All four directions must be trained equally — weakness in one causes injury
Move only the ankle — the leg stays still
Resistance should be challenging by rep 15-20
This is a daily practice — make it a pre-ice ritual
common_mistakes: Moving the entire leg instead of just the ankle
Only doing plantar flexion and dorsiflexion — skipping inversion/eversion
Band too light — no strengthening stimulus
target_elements: injury prevention — all elements, especially landings
drills.video_description: Skater performs complete ankle Theraband circuit — all four directions — demonstrating the comprehensive ankle strengthening essential for landing stability

drills.purpose: Improves jump height and range of motion by releasing the hip flexor for fuller leg swing
drills.repetitions: Hold each stretch 45 seconds, 3 sets each side
steps: Kneel on right knee, left foot forward in lunge position
Gently sink the hips forward and down toward the floor
Feel the stretch deep in the front of the right hip
Raise both arms overhead to deepen the stretch
Tilt slightly away from the kneeling leg to intensify
Hold for 45 seconds, breathing deeply
coach_cues: The hip flexor is the most common tight muscle in skaters — do this daily
A tight psoas steals 10-20cm from jump height — releasing it is immediate gain
Breathe OUT and sink deeper into the stretch on each exhale
If there is knee discomfort, place a folded mat under the kneeling knee
common_mistakes: Not sinking deep enough — the hip must go forward of the knee
Holding the breath — prevents the muscle from releasing
Only stretching the obvious quad stretch — not targeting the deep hip flexor
progressions: Add a gentle back arch for a full anterior chain stretch
target_elements: all jumps — swing leg range and height
drills.video_description: Skater demonstrates deep kneeling hip flexor stretch with arms overhead — releasing the psoas muscle that directly limits jump height when tight
